disclaimer: A planning aid, not financial, legal, or tax advice. Cadence math is arithmetic on your own inputs — posting more never guarantees views, revenue, or growth.

dealing_rules.basis: Same dealing arithmetic as the 90-Day Planner (assets/js/planner.js): long-form spreads across non-rest days by round-robin, shorts every other day; week 7 is the midpoint review.
rules: Long ideas are sorted by hook-strength score (highest first) before dealing — the best hooks earn the earliest weeks.
Longs deal round-robin across weeks: week 1 gets the top scores, not all of them at once.
Shorts and community ideas deal independently on their own cadence — they must never cannibalize a long slot.
Rest day is non-negotiable: no placement, analytics review only.
If ideas run out before slots, slots stay OPEN — never pad the calendar with filler. A visible gap is feedback: the bank needs ideas.
Surplus ideas stay in the bank as backlog — a full bank is a runway, not waste.
Week 7 (of 13) carries the midpoint review: kill the worst-performing format, double the best outlier.

batching.consistency_framing: Consistency beats volume — a cadence you can film is worth more than an ambitious one you abandon. The batching planner shows your film-day math honestly: if capacity doesn't cover cadence, shrink the cadence, don't promise yourself heroics.
guidance: Capacity = shoot_days_per_month × videos_per_shoot_day. Required = cadence × 52/12. Both are arithmetic on your own inputs.
A surplus means banked videos — publish steady, rest easy. A shortfall means a decision: add a shoot day, drop a slot, or merge formats.
Two short-form videos typically fit the effort of one long-form film block — budget shoot days by effort, not by count.
Never count 'I'll find the time' as capacity. Only scheduled, repeatable shoot days count.

repurposing_2_0.basis: Extends the wave-3 repurposing SOP (Phase 3, Everywhere Engine). The 2.0 map adds the full derivative map — every derivative must carry one original element (new hook, new framing, native caption). Repurposing is not re-uploading.

derivatives.effort: ~45 min each (edit for pacing, not re-upload)
derivatives.label: Short-form clip
derivatives.original_element: A fresh first 2 seconds — re-hook the clip, never reuse the pillar's intro
derivatives.task: Cut the best self-contained moment; burned-in captions, 9:16 reframe.

derivatives.label: Community reaction post
derivatives.original_element: A new question or poll written for the community tab — not the video title
derivatives.task: Post the debatable claim as a question or poll.

derivatives.label: TikTok cut
derivatives.task: Re-edit for TikTok pacing; keep 60–90s for Creator Rewards eligibility.
derivatives.original_element: Text-on-screen re-hook + native pacing — a re-edit, not a re-upload.

derivatives.label: Instagram Reel cut
derivatives.original_element: An aesthetic or save-worthy framing — transformation or reveal in the first 2 seconds
derivatives.task: Polished, save-worthy; caption as a mini-blog (5 hashtags).

derivatives.effort: ~1 hr (write the story around the numbers)
derivatives.label: Newsletter issue
derivatives.original_element: A written angle the video never states outright — the story behind the result
derivatives.task: Write the story around the video's numbers or result.

derivatives.label: X thread
derivatives.original_element: Written natively for X — first post is a new hook, not a link drop

derivatives.label: Facebook post
derivatives.task: Native upload of the best short as a Reel + discussion caption on your Page.
derivatives.original_element: A discussion-provoking caption ending with the debatable claim as a direct question.

repurposing_2_0.note: Cut 2–3 clips per pillar, not per platform — one clip per platform, each re-edited.

originality_guardrails.detail: The same video file uploaded to multiple platforms is distribution failure, not repurposing. Each derivative needs a native cut or a new hook.
A clip of the old intro dies on scroll. Every short-form derivative opens with a hook written for that platform.
originality_guardrails.rule: Every derivative gets a new hook

originality_guardrails.detail: Watermarks, letterboxed 16:9 on vertical, copy-pasted captions — platforms and viewers both punish it.
A community post that is just the video title is noise. Write the question the audience argues about.
originality_guardrails.rule: Text derivatives are written, not extracted

originality_guardrails.detail: If the pillar scores under 3/4 on the atom test (standalone hook, visual moment, quotable line, debatable claim), publish the pillar only — skip the repurposing and save the hours.
originality_guardrails.rule: Atom test gates the whole pipeline

deal_slots.description: Sponsored content slots reserved inside the content calendar. Pricing lives in the Deal Room and the 2026 rate card — the calendar only reserves the slots.
guidance: Reserve 1 slot per 4–6 organic pieces so sponsors never outnumber your own voice — an over-sponsored calendar bleeds trust.
Sponsor slots get the same hook-strength scoring as organic ideas; a weak sponsored video still costs you audience.
A sponsor slot is a calendar commitment, not a deal. Price it in the Deal Room (deal-room.html) before you promise it.
Links: the Deal Room (deal-room.html) for negotiation and the rate card (rate-card.html) for 2026 ranges.

simulator_bridge.description: Feed the calendar's cadence into the Empire Simulator as starting inputs. The simulator is a model, not a prediction.

algorithm_signals.research_basis: Wave-fuel research, Mission A (read 2026-10-11): TikTok algorithm (Hootsuite, Vamp, fivebbc, DMA, viral.app); YouTube Shorts Oct-1-2026 update (Creator Liaison Rene Ritchie via Social Media Today, Storyboard18, readus247); AI disclosure (aituber); Instagram Reels ranking (Virvid, CreatorFlow, SocialPilot, orangemonke, FlowShorts).

source_labels.platform-published: Stated by the platform itself (exec post, help docs, Creator Insider).
source_labels.single-source: One source only — treat as guidance, not law.
source_labels.creator-lore: Creator-community consensus, unverified by the platform — flagged.

platforms.label: TikTok — For You feed
platforms.optimize_for: Completion rate + watch time per impression.

mechanics.claim: Interest graph, not social graph — follower count is not a direct ranking factor.
Every upload is tested against a small matched audience pool (~300–500 accounts) and widened ~3–5x per wave only if early signals clear the gate.
Watch time per impression has replaced raw view counts — a 60-second video at 80% completion can outperform a 15-second clip at 95%.
The 'qualified view' bar may have risen from 3s to 5s in 2025–2026.
TikTok functions as a search engine — captions, on-screen text, and spoken keywords decide discoverability months later.
TikTok does not recommend reused, unoriginal, or engagement-bait content.
One agency estimates watch time/completion at 40–50% of ranking weight.

platforms.label: YouTube Shorts — recommendations feed
platforms.optimize_for: Completion rate (nobody clicks — they just don't swipe).

hierarchy.note: dominant; the metric that matters is completion rate, not CTR
a declining signal on swipe-driven feeds

mechanics.claim: Oct 1, 2026 update: Shorts recommendations prioritize original content and reduce reach for re-uploaded material 'without adding anything of your own'.
mechanics.source: Rene Ritchie (Creator Liaison), Creator Insider video + TeamYouTube community post, Oct 1 2026; reported by Social Media Today, Storyboard18, readus247

mechanics.claim: The judgment is at the channel level: channels that primarily aggregate or re-upload without significant changes likely see less distribution — clipping channels are the direct target.
Recommendations only, not monetization — reach is cut; payout formulas are unchanged.
Real commentary, unique edits, or storytelling keep a channel safe; reaction and quoting with genuine added perspective are explicitly carved out.
mechanics.source: Ritchie announcement via Social Media Today

mechanics.claim: AI disclosure (May 2026 enforcement): automated detection flags undisclosed photorealistic AI content; properly labeled videos get normal distribution — AI labels alone don't affect recommendations or pay. Undisclosed ones face reduced recommendations or removal.
Shorts-specific search filters launched in 2026 — keyword SEO matters for short-form for the first time.
Retention thresholds around ~65% (sub-30s) / ~50% (30–60s) keep a Short in distribution.

platforms.label: Instagram Reels
platforms.optimize_for: Sends per reach — build Reels people want to send someone.

hierarchy.note: Mosseri: correlates with reach more than watch time or likes
likes matter more for connected (follower) content; sends dominate unconnected discovery

mechanics.claim: 'Sends are worth 3–5x a like' is an invented number with no source — Instagram publishes no weights.
Most Reels impressions come from accounts the viewer doesn't follow; ~100 Reels are scored for 'Reels chaining'.
Reels longer than ~3 minutes are reportedly not pushed to non-followers; 7–30 seconds is the discovery sweet spot.
TikTok watermarks are explicitly deprioritized; low-resolution and engagement-bait content are penalized.

hook_patterns.basis: Structural hook patterns distilled from the October 2026 TikTok trend reports (SocialPilot, New Engen, Later, MediaNug, Virlo, Lightreel — read 2026-10-11). Trends expire in weeks; the containers below — reveal, confession, contrast — keep working. Steal the structure, never the sound or the exact format.
hook_patterns.honesty_note: These are patterns, not predictions. A structure improves your odds; it never guarantees views.

patterns.name: The Costume Reveal Walk
patterns.formula: Open on a striking walk toward the camera — low angle, full commitment — then the zoom-out reveals the transformation.
patterns.mechanic: Completion + watch time: the promised visual reveal is an open loop; viewers stay to see the payoff.
patterns.spotted_in: Ramalama Costume Walk — 430.7K videos (SocialPilot, Sept 25–Oct 5, 2026; New Engen)
patterns.adapt: The walk is a container. Swap the costume for your reveal: the finished product, the before/after, the result of the experiment.

patterns.name: The Leaving Edit
patterns.formula: 'I left [X] behind' — a confession montage of walking away from a habit, job, or belief, cut to a wistful track.
patterns.mechanic: Sends + shares: an identity confession people DM to friends ('this is so you').
patterns.spotted_in: Patient Zero edits — wedding edits and 'leaving something behind' audio, 149.3K videos (SocialPilot; Virlo, Oct 2026)
patterns.adapt: Works for any transformation arc in your niche: the diet you quit, the tool you dropped, the belief you outgrew.

patterns.name: The Joy Contrast
patterns.formula: Upbeat, happy-dance energy layered over chaos — the track and the caption contradict each other.
patterns.mechanic: Rewatches + comments: the contradiction makes viewers watch twice and comment 'same'.
patterns.spotted_in: Be OK / 'I just want to be OK' — happy-dance-over-chaos (New Engen; Later, Oct 2, 2026)
patterns.adapt: Pair your realest caption with your most upbeat 3 seconds. The clash is the hook.

patterns.name: The Hidden Confession
patterns.formula: 'Text from -A' framing: 'POV: someone just exposed the thing I've been hiding about [X].'
patterns.mechanic: Watch time + comments: social tension creates a stay-to-the-end promise; the comments become the confessional.
patterns.adapt: Confess a niche truth your audience thinks they're alone in. Specificity beats drama.

patterns.name: The Cozy Bed
patterns.formula: Romanticize a routine: slow shots of the ordinary process, a jazz/piano bed underneath, text overlay naming the ordinary thing as the good thing.
patterns.mechanic: Saves + search: save-for-later comfort content; keyword-rich captions ride TikTok search.
patterns.spotted_in: Cozy-fall mood beds — 5 of Metricool's Oct 1, 2026 top-10 sounds are jazz/piano/ambient (Virlo)
patterns.adapt: Any 'day in my process' content becomes a save magnet with the right bed and a keyword-forward caption.

patterns.name: The Upside-Down Flip
patterns.formula: Shoot the 'before' upside down or mid-gesture; flip to the 'after' on the beat — the transition IS the hook.
patterns.mechanic: Completion + shares: the visual trick delays the payoff past the swipe point.
patterns.adapt: Use for any transformation: edits, builds, makeovers, data reveals. Film the flip, not the filter.

adaptation_matrix.basis: Platform-native adaptation, not blind cross-posting. One clip, four dialects. Under the Oct-1-2026 rules every destination needs at least one original element — a re-cut opening, a re-recorded voiceover, a new text overlay, or a new caption angle. Grammars from Phase 3 (The Everywhere Engine).

tiktok>shorts: Re-cut the opening: the first 2 seconds must carry the payoff — Shorts is swipe-driven, no title or CTR to save you.
Strip or rebuild the TikTok text overlay — Shorts viewers expect burned-in captions, not TikTok's UI text.
Loop the ending into the opening when the format allows — loopable Shorts harvest rewatches.
AI disclosure: if the clip uses photorealistic AI, apply YouTube's AI-content label BEFORE upload — labeled gets normal distribution (Ritchie, May 2026; aituber).
Swap trending TikTok audio for a Shorts-safe track whenever you don't hold the rights cross-platform.
tiktok>reels: Strip the TikTok watermark — watermarked re-uploads are explicitly deprioritized on Reels (FlowShorts). Export a clean master from your editor.
Re-edit for polish: Reels rewards aesthetic consistency — stabilize, grade, reframe.
Rewrite the caption as a mini-blog + ~5 hashtags (Reels grammar, not TikTok's keyword-stuffed caption).
Add the send trigger: a 'send this to someone who…' CTA or a quotable line built for DMs — sends per reach is Mosseri's #1 signal.
Keep it under ~3 minutes — longer Reels reportedly aren't pushed to non-followers (orangemonke, single source).
tiktok>facebook: Write a discussion-prompting caption ending in a direct question — Facebook's algorithm weights meaningful discussion.
Native upload to your Page; never post the TikTok link.
Slightly longer is fine here — Facebook rewards native long-ish video, so keep the fuller cut, not the trimmed one.
Respect Meta's March 2026 repost policy: your own content with native captions is normal practice; reposting others' videos kills reach.
shorts>tiktok: Add TikTok-native text-on-screen hooks — TikTok grammar is raw, fast, text-forward.
Say your keywords out loud in the first 10 seconds, in on-screen text, and in the caption — TikTok is a search engine; Shorts SEO doesn't transfer.
Keep 60–90 seconds when the format allows to stay Creator Rewards eligible (1 min+, original, 10K followers / 100K views in 30d).
Strip YouTube end-cards and subscribe CTAs — they read as off-platform on TikTok.
shorts>reels: Export a clean master — no watermarks or cross-platform branding.
Polish pass: aesthetic reframe + save-worthy framing (transformation or reveal in the first 2 seconds).
Caption as mini-blog + hashtags; add the DM-send trigger.
Keep it under ~3 minutes for discovery; save longer cuts for followers.
shorts>facebook: Native upload to your Page — Facebook rewards long-ish native video, so bring the fuller cut.
Write a discussion-prompting caption with a direct question.
Post the best short as a Facebook Reel too.
reels>tiktok: De-polish: faster pacing, rawer cuts — TikTok's grammar rewards authenticity over aesthetic.
Replace the mini-blog caption with keyword-forward text, and say the keywords on camera.
Re-hook the first 2 seconds with a native text overlay.
reels>shorts: Tighten the hook to the first 2 seconds — Shorts viewers decide faster than Reels scrollers.
Burn in captions if the Reel relied on Instagram's auto-captions.
Apply YouTube's AI-content label if the Reel used photorealistic AI — labeled gets normal distribution.
Loop the ending into the opening when the format allows.
reels>facebook: Native upload to your Page with a discussion-prompting caption.
The polished aesthetic transfers fine — Facebook audiences skew older and appreciate production value.
Keep the mini-blog caption's best line as the discussion question.
facebook>tiktok: Cut down: Facebook's longer cut must become a 60–90s TikTok cut with a brand-new hook.
Add text-on-screen overlay and keyword delivery for TikTok search.
facebook>shorts: Extract the best self-contained moment — a Facebook cut is rarely a Short as-is.
Re-hook the first 2 seconds; 9:16 reframe; burned-in captions.
Apply YouTube's AI-content label if the footage used photorealistic AI.
facebook>reels: Export a clean master — no watermarks.
Polish pass: aesthetic reframe; mini-blog caption + hashtags + the DM-send trigger.
Keep it under ~3 minutes for discovery.

universal_checks: Upload native, every time. Watermarks from another platform are deprioritized (TikTok watermark on Reels is explicit). Export a clean master from your editor.
9:16 full-frame. Letterboxed 16:9 on vertical reads as recycled — platforms and viewers both punish it.
A new hook per destination. Same file, same first 2 seconds = a re-upload, not repurposing — and the Oct-1 rules starve re-uploads.
One original element minimum per destination (re-cut opening, re-recorded VO, new text overlay, new caption angle). 'Repurposing is not re-uploading' is policy now, not advice.
Photorealistic AI? Disclose on YouTube before upload (labeled = normal distribution; hiding = reduced reach or removal). Other platforms: check the current disclosure rules — they move.
Stagger posting across days. The same idea everywhere on the same day splits your own audience's attention and looks automated.
adaptation_matrix.oct1_gate: Oct-1-2026 gate: YouTube's Shorts update judges at the CHANNEL level — channels that primarily re-upload without adding anything of their own get less distribution (Ritchie, Oct 1 2026). TikTok demotes reused/unoriginal content; Meta's March 2026 policy targets reposts with low-value changes. Every adaptation below adds the original element that keeps you on the right side of all three.

batching_scheduler.basis: Input your weekly hours → the scheduler blocks film / edit / publish time against your cadence and tells you whether the week holds. Default task minutes are adjustable starting estimates, NOT benchmarks — your footage, your edit speed, your reality.
guidance: Film day, edit day, publish day — blocks in that order. Never edit what you haven't filmed; never publish what you haven't edited.
Required hours = cadence × your per-task minutes. If the week doesn't hold, change the inputs you control — cadence, hours, or per-task time — not your standards.
One rest day is non-negotiable. A schedule with no rest day is a plan to quit.
Publish blocks include packaging (title, thumbnail, captions, scheduling) — the invisible 30% most creators forget to budget.
